title: OHA celebrates three decades serving Fredericksburg area homeowners - Fredericksburg Leader
text:
A ribbon cutting ceremony was held on February 12 by the Fredericksburg Regional Chamber of Commerce to mark the 30th anniversary of OHA HVAC, Plumbing, Chimney & Fireplaces. The company started as an HVAC provider and has since expanded its services to include plumbing, roofing, chimney and fireplace maintenance, generators, water heaters, and indoor air quality solutions.
OHA is a family-owned business that emphasizes reliable service for homeowners in the area. According to the company’s statement: “Being a family-owned and community-oriented business, OHA takes great pride in delivering expert care and trustworthy service to homeowners—always On-Time, Honest, and Affordable.”
The event featured remarks from Spotsylvania County Economic Development Director Kevin Marshall. Lori Hayes (Chairman), Board of Supervisor from the Lee Hill District, also spoke at the ceremony. David Goosman from the Berkeley District Board of Supervisors attended as well.
OHA is located at 3341 Shannon Park Drive in Fredericksburg.
Spotsylvania County continues to see changes in its public school enrollment. During the 2023-24 school year, Spotsylvania County Public Schools enrolled 24,064 students across its district. This represented a slight decrease of 0.8% compared to the previous year’s total enrollment of 24,260 students (https://www.doe.virginia.gov/home). Riverbend High School had the highest enrollment among county schools with 1,953 students during this period (https://www.doe.virginia.gov/home).
Demographic data show that white students made up 43.8% of Spotsylvania County’s public school population with 10,540 students enrolled in 2023-24; Hispanic students followed at 24.3%, totaling 5,851 students (https://www.doe.virginia.gov/home).
Cedar Forest Elementary School had the largest pre-kindergarten enrollment in the county with 86 children representing about one-fifth of all pre-kindergarteners locally (https://www.doe.virginia.gov/home). Parkside Elementary led kindergarten enrollments with 170 students or roughly one-tenth of all kindergartners in Spotsylvania County for that year (https://www.doe.virginia.gov/home).
To view a video of the ribbon cutting event visit OHA’s website.
